newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates ends down, spot up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates ends down, spot up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Tuesday with money supply ample due to a dearth of new domestic A share issues and listings, traders said.
But the most active three-day contract rose to 6.5 percent from 5.0 percent on A share market gains, they said.
Combined market turnover fell to 3.36 million lots from 6.64 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said a break in A share issues and listings on the stock markets had resulted in institutions placing large amounts of cash on the repo markets, leading to an over-supply.
But successive gains on the domestic A share markets were supporting the three-day contract, they said.
Traders said they expect the trend to continue on Wednesday.
"I believe the rates will move in a narrow range in the next few days due to a lack of new A issues and listings," one said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Tuesday but traders said prices seemed to have met resistance after a few days of solid gains.
The most active three-year notes that matures in August 1999 rose to 105.43 yuan from 105.22 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 0.88 million lots from 2.62 million.
Traders said yields of the contracts had dropped significantly after rises in the past few trading days and the market would have a technical rebound in the short term.
"Technical charts have indicated that the contracts will have a technical correction this week," said one trader. "But potential for losses is limited because of strong market fundamentals."
